clue.text: Declare girl has put weight on

blocks.note: a common girl's name
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A young woman announces, perhaps ruefully, that she has gained some weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a girl putting on weight; cryptically the weight is simply placed after the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something is to make it public, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Recess found among cheap seats

indicators.note: something found among other things is sitting inside them, here within the next words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: An alcove turns up among the low-priced seats in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted semicircular recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: Fastidious resort

blocks.note: first meaning: precise, finely discriminating
second meaning: the French Riviera holiday town

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective can mean subtle or exacting, its older sense; it is also the Riviera city on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Made one of the team

blocks.note: first meaning: joined together
second meaning: the name of many football clubs, such as Manchester's

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as selection for a side; the second sense is the word many British football clubs carry in their names, such as Manchester or Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Things joined into a single whole have been unified, and the word also names numerous sports clubs.

clue.text: Taking into account motive

blocks.note: first meaning: careful thought about something
second meaning: a reason or inducement for doing something

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means careful thought given to factors, and also a reason or payment prompting action, as in for a consideration.

clue.text: Author holding leading post at university

indicators.note: whatever holds something keeps it inside, so the author's name wraps around the other piece
the leading part of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: Albert Camus, the French novelist
first letter of post

explanation.surface: A writer is appointed to a top job at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Camus, author of The Outsider, is a favourite crossword author because his name splits so readily.
explanation.definitionFit: The campus is the grounds and buildings of a university, so the word stands for the institution itself by association.

clue.text: Refrains from making sailors accept taint of guilt

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the sailors surround the other piece

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual sailor; plural here
a stain is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to make seamen take on any trace of guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstains means deliberately holds back from doing something, a verb synonym for refrains.

clue.text: Foretold about one that made affirmation

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the number

blocks.note: predicted means foretold
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone prophesied the arrival of a person who would make a solemn declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: To predicate is to assert or affirm something as true, so predicated means affirmed.

clue.text: State of inertia in country without females?

blocks.note: a stag party is a men-only celebration
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A country with no women might fall into lethargy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the joke: a stag nation would have no women and so, presumably, no growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a condition of no movement, growth or development.

clue.text: It is stirred into barbiturate in parts

indicators.note: stirring mixes things around, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled
putting something into another thing places it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Seconal is a brand-name barbiturate sedative
the two letters of it, mixed

explanation.surface: Something is mixed into a sedative drug, given in separate doses.
explanation.walkthrough: Seconal is a trade name for the barbiturate secobarbital; the jumbled IT sits after its first three letters: SEC-TI-ONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sectional is made or divided into separate sections, so it comes in parts.

clue.text: One having meal out at spot where nuclear attack might start

indicators.note: having can mean holding, so the eating word takes in the number

blocks.note: lunching is having a midday meal, often away from home
a means one
a site is a spot or place

explanation.surface: Someone eats out at the very place a nuclear strike could be fired from.
explanation.definitionFit: A launching site is the base from which missiles are fired, so it is where an attack begins.

clue.text: Queen having to keep silent about American president

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the president's name is read the other way

blocks.note: the sound used to tell someone to be quiet
Abe is Abraham Lincoln's nickname

explanation.surface: A monarch must say nothing on the subject of a US president.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen of Sheba is the biblical ruler who visited King Solomon, so the name alone fits a queen clue.

clue.text: Cult that is, perhaps, about to apply restrictions to network

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged otherwise, inviting a reshuffle
about means surrounding, so the restricting word goes round the mixed letters

blocks.note: taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
to ration something is to limit how much may be had

explanation.surface: A sect is about to impose limits on its network of members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like a hedge in the surface, but it is what tells you to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticulation is a net-like pattern or arrangement of lines, a more technical word for network.

clue.text: Relating to the jaw featured in bird manual

indicators.note: featured in suggests the letters are worked into a new form rather than kept as they stand

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A bird guidebook has a section about jaws.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a word hidden in the guide, but the letters are rearranged, not hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandible is the lower jawbone, so the adjective means pertaining to the jaw.

clue.text: Enough to live on comfortably, given fitness

blocks.note: first meaning: a sufficient income
second meaning: ability, capability

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old term for a comfortable income, and it also means capability or suitability for a task.

clue.text: Travel back to Georgia in eager excitement

indicators.note: going back means heading the other way, so the combined letters are read from the end

blocks.note: to go is to travel
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled to be returning to Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agog means being keen and eagerly expectant, an adjective close in sense to excited.

clue.text: Offspring of central figure in Dante''s "Inferno"?

blocks.note: first meaning: a child or later member of a family line
second meaning: the poem's narrator goes down through the circles of Hell, so he is one who goes downward

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: Dante spends the Inferno going down into Hell, so he is literally one who descends.
explanation.definitionFit: A descendant is someone's offspring or later family member, and punningly anyone travelling downwards.

clue.text: A hundred too old to get press write-up?

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
over age means past the age limit

explanation.surface: A centenarian is too old to be written up in the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the reporting given to an event by newspapers and broadcasters.

clue.text: It may be tactful to take degree with small movement

blocks.note: a diploma is a qualification, loosely a degree
a tic is a small involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Someone suggests the polite course is to accept a qualification with a modest gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Being diplomatic means handling people with sensitivity and skill, a near synonym for tactful.

clue.text: Queen accepted by no emperor

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so the queen sits inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: No emperor would welcome a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was the notorious Roman ruler said to have fiddled while Rome burned.

clue.text: Fellow, for example, getting early start in art of horsemanship

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
first letter of early

explanation.surface: A man, say, gets an early start in learning to ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Manege is the training of horses and riders in dressage, and also the riding school where it happens.

clue.text: Weapon that would be deplored by the RSPCA

definitions.text: Weapon that would be deplored by the RSPCA

blocks.note: surface reading: a siege engine, a weapon of war
setter's reading: an animal charity would object to beating a male sheep

explanation.walkthrough: The RSPCA is the Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals, Britain's animal welfare charity; read the answer as a verb and a male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy beam used to break down gates and doors is a siege weapon of ancient warfare.

clue.text: Band requiring agent

blocks.note: first meaning: a tie or binding
second meaning: James ..., the fictional secret agent

explanation.surface: A music group needs someone to manage its bookings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is something that ties or binds, like a band, and James Bond is the famous fictional spy.

clue.text: One seeing flyers return from a good way off

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the flyers are read the other way

blocks.note: a means one
the RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's air arm

explanation.surface: Someone watches pilots coming home from a great distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or from a long distance, the adverb used in phrases like seen from afar.

clue.text: Girl (backward) appears to notice nothing

indicators.note: backward means facing the other way, so the pieces are read right to left

blocks.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A shy girl seems to notice nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a common woman's name, so it fits a clue asking for a girl.

clue.text: What players often hear from wings sounds bad

definitions.text: What players often hear from wings

blocks.note: noises are sounds
food that is off has gone bad

explanation.surface: Footballers in wide positions hear unpleasant sounds from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Players and wings suggest a sports pitch, but they are actors and the sides of a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises off are sound effects made offstage, a theatre term for what actors hear from the wings.

clue.text: Staggered by Spanish article about grass

indicators.note: about here signals one item placed around the other, so the grass wraps the article

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone was shocked by a Spanish piece of writing about grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Read strictly, 'article about grass' would put the article outside; here it is the grass that goes round the article, a loose use of 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeled means lurched unsteadily, the past tense of a verb close to staggered.

clue.text: He is there to protect back, for example

blocks.note: first meaning: a guardian or protector
second meaning: a full back in football is one of the team's rear players

explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a verb meaning support, but it is a football position.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian who protects, and in team sports a back is a player whose role is stopping opponents scoring.
